definitions.explanation: A vivid, bright shade of red. One of Japan's traditional colors, historically associated with nobility and high rank.

examples.japanese: {紅葉|もみじ}が{緋色|ひいろ}に{色|いろ}づいた。
{緋色|ひいろ}の{袴|はかま}を{身|み}にまとった{巫女|みこ}が{境内|けいだい}を{歩|ある}いている。
examples.english: A shrine maiden wearing scarlet hakama is walking through the shrine grounds.

notes:
A vivid bright red, one of Japan's traditional colors. The character {緋|ひ} specifically refers to this shade of red and is rarely used outside of color descriptions.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {緋色|ひいろ}の{着物|きもの}: scarlet kimono
- {緋色|ひいろ}の{袴|はかま}: scarlet hakama (worn by shrine maidens)
- {緋色|ひいろ}に{染|そ}まる: to turn scarlet

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {茜色|あかねいろ}: madder red — a warmer, more orange-tinged red
- {朱色|しゅいろ}: vermilion — a brighter, more orange shade
- {紅色|べにいろ}: crimson — a deeper, cooler red
- {真|ま}っ{赤|か}: bright red — everyday word for vivid red

CULTURAL NOTE:
In traditional Japan, {緋色|ひいろ} was associated with high social rank. The scarlet {袴|はかま} worn by {巫女|みこ} (shrine maidens) is one of the most recognizable examples. The color also appears in the Japanese title of Arthur Conan Doyle's "A Study in Scarlet" ({緋色|ひいろ}の{研究|けんきゅう}).
